items.title: Live PostgreSQL/pgvector proof
items.objective: Replace the single PostgreSQL-only skip with reproducible live integration evidence.
acceptance: FORCE RLS isolation proven for documents/versions/spans/embeddings
backup restores into a new database
schema parity and audit head pass
items.execution_note: api:postgres-and-restore runs the suite against a migrated PostgreSQL 17 with a non-superuser role and restores an encrypted dump into a fresh database; 430 tests and the RLS isolation checks pass there. What remains is pgvector under load and a cluster nobody here operates.

items.title: Immutable software supply chain
items.objective: Make every Python, container and CI dependency content-addressed and verifiable.
items.execution_note: Both lock files carry sha256 for all 68 artefacts, every install site passes --require-hashes, and every image in the pipeline, the compose file and both Dockerfiles is pinned by digest. SUP-002 and SUP-001 are CLOSED_LOCAL. Signed build provenance and immutable registry promotion remain external.

items.title: Real-corpus TEVV and calibration
items.objective: Replace synthetic-only evidence with blinded, adjudicated corpus-specific evaluation.
acceptance: blind holdout never used for tuning
items.execution_note: The frozen eval is 30 fixture observations with a 0.114-wide interval and no declared corpus; it reports admissible_as_tevv=false for exactly that reason. Real-corpus TEVV needs annotated queries and an independent assessor.

items.title: Ukrainian retrieval and structured evidence
items.objective: Improve Ukrainian morphology and prove table/number/unit/formula handling.
items.execution_note: numeric_integrity.py and table_integrity.py detect the extraction failures that leave text looking clean; they join the review gate rather than filling a field. Formula structure and layout-aware table recovery remain.

items.title: Risk and injection model replacement
items.objective: Replace regex-only risk and injection classification with measurable layered controls.
acceptance: no control text reaches instruction channel
items.execution_note: risk_rules.py carries ids, rationales and its own examples, and an unmatched query is UNCLASSIFIED scored at the stricter setting rather than falling to the loosest one. A trained classifier on a blind set with per-class metrics remains.

items.title: Repository and configuration decomposition
items.objective: Split god objects without weakening transactions, RLS or audit invariants.
acceptance: repository responsibilities split by bounded capability
no broad exception in critical path without rethrow policy
items.execution_note: SqlRepository 1855 -> 1047 across four extractions (audit_reader, row_mapping, schema, retrieval_queries), held by a line/complexity ratchet and seam tests that assert the query builders never open a connection. validate_security_and_calibration 103 -> 57 and validate_infrastructure.main 102 -> 5. The transactional core is deliberately not split: CRUD, review, audit append and readiness share one transaction.

items.title: Embedding lifecycle and drift
items.objective: Make embedding synchronization, model migration and rollback explicit and auditable.
acceptance: drift threshold opens incident and disables semantic weight when violated
items.execution_note: embedding_coverage.py distinguishes four index states and embedding_migration.py plans a resumable blue-green move with switch/retire/rollback admissibility. Executing it against a real index and embedding service remains.

items.title: Retention, deletion and legal hold execution
items.objective: Convert corpus policy fields into scheduled, reconciled lifecycle operations.
acceptance: evidence retention policy executed and audited
items.execution_note: retention.py computes a disposition per document and plan_retention.py reconciles it against storage. It deletes nothing and is not a timer: AWAITING_DECISION exists because keeping expired material quietly reports a clean posture over something nobody ruled on. Executing deletions needs an owner's decision.

items.title: SRE capacity, chaos and recovery proof
items.objective: Turn reference topology into measured service limits and recovery guarantees.
items.execution_note: recovery.py classifies an RTO/RPO claim (MISSING / INCOMPLETE_PROVENANCE / OVERSTATED_SCALE / FIXTURE_SCALE / MEASURED) and environment_drift.py compares a desired state against an observed environment with UNOBSERVED kept apart from IN_SYNC. Both are refusals about evidence, not evidence: load, soak, chaos and a measured recovery on production-scale data remain external.

items.title: Independent security and authorization closure
items.objective: Produce evidence the repository cannot self-issue: independent tests and formal go/no-go.
acceptance: all applicable P0 closed or formally time-bounded with compensating controls
production_authorized becomes true only through signed external evidence
items.execution_note: attestors.py verifies Ed25519 attestations against enrolled keys and admission is computed from admission-grounds.json rather than asserted, so an external assessment can no longer be granted by editing the tree. The registry ships empty, which is the honest state: no independent assessment has been received.

status_note: Read this as eight of ten started and none finished. Every PARTIALLY_EXECUTED item has code that runs and a test that fails without it; not one of them has met its own acceptance list, because every list ends in evidence from a system nobody here operates — a cluster, an assessor, an annotated corpus, a risk owner. The register read PLANNED_NOT_EXECUTED until 2026-08-05 while eight items had shipped, which is the same defect the closure counts had: a document about progress that had not closed its own loop.
